record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Function Field Arithmetic — The Influence of John Tate’s Work
record.context_brief: Orders of vanishing at negative integers
record.original_question: What is the correct general description of the orders of vanishing of function-field zeta functions at negative integers, including an explanation of the systematic extra-vanishing phenomena that depend on the digit combinatorics of the integer s and on Weierstrass gaps?

evidence.quote: Classically, a simple analysis of poles of gamma factors occurring in the functional equations of general zeta functions leads to determination of orders of vanishing of zeta functions at negative integers. In function fields, the story is not even conjecturally fully understood. There is some interesting systematic ‘extra vanishing’ phenomena of zeta at −s depending on digit combinatorics of s and Weierstrass gaps [Tha04, Sec. 5.4] and [Gos].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a global function field with field of constants $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $\zeta_K(s)$ denote the associated Goss zeta function (a characteristic-$p$ analogue of the Dedekind zeta function, taking values in a Tate algebra and admitting an analytic continuation to a "complex plane" $\mathbb{C}_\infty^* \times \mathbb{Z}_p$). For each negative integer $-s$ (with $s$ a positive integer), $\zeta_K$ vanishes at $-s$, and beyond the "naive" order of vanishing predicted by an analogue of the gamma-factor analysis used in the classical case, additional systematic "extra vanishing" is known to occur. This extra vanishing depends in a subtle way on:
\begin{itemize}
\item the combinatorics of the base-$q$ digits of the positive integer $s$, and
\item the Weierstrass gap sequence at the place at infinity (or more generally, the Weierstrass gaps of $K$).
\end{itemize}

Problem. Give a correct general formula or conjectural description for the exact order of vanishing $\mathrm{ord}_{s=-n}\,\zeta_K(s)$ at every negative integer $-n$, valid for arbitrary global function fields $K/\mathbb{F}_q$, that simultaneously accounts for:
(i) the trivial zeros coming from the gamma-factor / functional-equation analogy,
(ii) the extra zeros depending on the $q$-adic digit combinatorics of $n$, and
(iii) the contribution of the Weierstrass gaps of $K$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general description of orders of vanishing of function-field (Goss) zeta functions at negative integers, including the systematic extra-vanishing tied to base-$q$ digit combinatorics and Weierstrass gaps, remains not fully understood even conjecturally. Partial results exist (e.g., Thakur's sufficient conditions for orders of vanishing for $\mathbb{F}_2$ and principal-ideal cases; Sheats, Diaz-Vargas, and others on $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$; recent work on multizeta vanishing at negative integers showing only trivial zeros occur in that setting), but no complete general formula is established.

status_evidence.title: Orders of vanishing of zeros of characteristic p zeta function
status_evidence.snippet: Thakur gives sufficient conditions for orders of vanishing of zeros of the absolute zeta function in the case of two-element field, principal ideals.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial sufficient conditions are known; the general picture is incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Vanishing of Multiple Zeta Values over Fq[t] at Negative Integers
status_evidence.snippet: At negative integers, trivial zeros account for all vanishing of multizeta values over Fq[t]; results focus on the polynomial ring case.
status_evidence.claim: General function-field case (with Weierstrass gaps) not addressed; only Fq[t] resolved for multizeta.
